transcript.content: Hello, welcome to the clinic. Can you tell me what brings you in today?

Yeah, um… I came in because I can’t shut my brain off anymore. It starts with one thing, like a client not responding to an email, and then suddenly I’m running through this whole chain in my head—like, okay, they’re upset, we’re going to lose the contract, then I’ll fall behind on my divorce payments, and then I’m never going to get back into a real leadership role again.

And I know that probably sounds like a lot from just one unanswered message, but that’s kind of the problem. It just takes off. I manage information systems, so I’m used to thinking through contingencies, you know, like if one server goes down, what’s the failover plan—but this is different. It’s like my brain treats everything like a crisis plan, even when it’s just… a client being slow to reply.
Do you find that you worry excessively about a variety of things in your life, not just work-related issues or specific events, and does this worry feel difficult to control?

Yeah, it’s not just work. Work is the easiest example because it has names and emails and deadlines attached to it, but my mind jumps all over the place. One minute it’s contract work, then it’s the mortgage, then it’s whether people in the Bethesda tech circles think I’m, I don’t know, damaged goods or something.

And the stupidest little thing can set it off. Like if a recruiter doesn’t answer an email right away, part of me knows they’re probably just busy, but my brain goes, “That’s it, your career is closing down.” And then I’m already five steps ahead, thinking about money and reputation and everything falling apart. It’s… hard to pull it back once it starts.
Do you notice any physical sensations when these worries come up, like restlessness, muscle tension, or trouble relaxing?

Yeah, definitely. I feel kind of wound up almost all day, like I’m braced for something. My shoulders get locked up—like I’m sitting there waiting for bad news even if nothing’s actually happening.

And I’ll catch myself pacing around the house, or on work calls I’m bouncing my leg under the desk the whole time. Sometimes I don’t even notice I’m doing it until I realize I’ve been walking from the kitchen to the office and back for no real reason. It’s like my body is reacting to some crisis that hasn’t happened.
Have you been feeling down, hopeless, or losing interest in things you used to enjoy, even when there’s no immediate stressor or worry to trigger it?

I’m not sure I’d call it hopeless, exactly. I mean, I get discouraged, but usually it’s tied to something my brain has already grabbed onto and started turning into a whole scenario.

As far as losing interest… I don’t know. I haven’t really been tracking it that way. Sometimes I don’t do things I used to do, but then I’ll think, well, is that because I don’t enjoy them, or because I’m sitting there checking email or thinking about some conversation from three days ago? It kind of all blends together.

Sorry, that probably doesn’t answer it cleanly. I guess I haven’t noticed a separate thing where I’m just down for no reason. It’s more… when I get stuck on something, everything else gets pushed out.
Have you had times when you felt down or low that didn’t seem connected to any particular worry or event, just coming out of the blue?

I don’t really know. I mean, not that I can clearly point to. Usually if I feel low, I can trace it back to something I’ve been chewing on, even if it’s something small that got bigger in my head.

But “out of the blue”… I’m trying to think. Sometimes I’ll wake up already kind of heavy, but then I’ll realize I’m thinking about some email I didn’t answer or something someone said, or I’ll check my phone before I’m even fully awake, which is probably not helping. My wife tells me I do that too much—sorry, that’s not really what you asked.

So, no, I haven’t really noticed low moods just appearing on their own. It’s more like they come attached to whatever my mind is stuck on.
Do you find yourself feeling anxious and worrying almost every day, even when there isn’t a specific event or problem that your mind is focused on?

Yeah… pretty much every day. It doesn’t always start with one clear thing, it’s more like my mind is scanning for something to latch onto.

Like I’ll be trying to get coffee and suddenly I’m thinking about contract work, then the mortgage, then whether people in the Bethesda tech circles are talking about me like I’m damaged goods. And then if a recruiter takes too long to answer an email, my brain turns that into, “Well, that’s it, your career is basically closing down.”

Which sounds dramatic when I say it out loud, but in the moment it feels very real. It just jumps around, even when there isn’t one specific crisis happening.
When your mind gets stuck on these worries, do you feel a need to keep moving, like you can't sit still, or feel like you're on edge in a way that's more intense than just feeling tense?

Yeah, I do. I mean, I don’t know if I’d describe it as needing to move exactly, but I’m kind of wound up almost all day. Like my shoulders are locked up and I’m just waiting for bad news to come in.

I’ll pace around the house without realizing it, especially if I’m thinking through something, or I’ll be on a call and my leg is bouncing the whole time. Sometimes nothing is even happening—no new email, no phone call, no actual problem right then—but my body acts like there is. It’s like I’m braced for something.
